verdict.rationale: npm's docs show it installs packages from the public registry with `npm install <name>`, lets you browse everything there with `npm search`, and lets you point at any compatible registry or run your own. Community reports of a flood of published packages and multi-million monthly download counts support the 'large' part of the story. Supply-chain security complaints concern trust, not whether packages are available, so they do not contradict the capability. Missing for 10: first-party evidence of registry size or package count, explicit evidence of active maintenance across the registry.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install almost anything I need from a large, actively maintained package registry or repository

citations.quote: You can also run `npm install blerg` to install the latest version of "blerg".
Use the `npm search` command to show everything that's available in the public registry.
You can configure npm to use any compatible registry you like, and even run your own registry.
Per npm download stats, 2,538,464 of left-pad's 2,550,569 monthly downloads came via the line-numbers package.
